lab.title: Optional manual lab: inspect a sandbox account and preview a safe upload
lab.purpose: Observe account configuration, Microsoft Entra Blob authorization, and an AzCopy dry run without provisioning Azure resources, enabling replication, changing encryption keys, or deleting shared data.
prerequisites: This lab is optional. An instructor must approve use of an existing disposable standard general-purpose v2 account with a flat namespace and provide its exact subscription, resource group, account, and isolated manual-transfer-demo container.
Use only synthetic text. The container must not hold real school records or participate in object replication, immutability, or another production workflow.

Have a current Storage Explorer and AzCopy v10 installation, the correct tenant ID, a permitted network path, and a narrow Storage Blob Data Contributor assignment on the lab container. Management Reader is needed only if inspecting account configuration through the portal.
The instructor must explain any existing versioning or soft-delete retention and authorize the precise demo-object cleanup. Do not retrieve or share account keys or signed access URLs.
lab.costWarning: Existing storage is not necessarily free. Uploads, listings, downloads, dry-run enumeration, retained versions or soft-deleted data, and network transfer may incur charges. Do not create accounts, private endpoints, Key Vaults, encryption scopes, replication policies, or premium resources for this exercise. Skip the lab if a suitable approved sandbox is unavailable.
steps: Manually inspect the supplied account in the portal, if authorized. Record kind, performance, redundancy, region, namespace, encryption type, and secure-transfer setting without changing them. Do not display access keys.
On paper, compare the account with the first lesson's Standard_ZRS plan. Explain any difference, such as a disposable LRS sandbox that intentionally does not provide zonal resilience.

Sign into Storage Explorer with the approved tenant and identity. Disable optional account-key usage for the Blob exercise. Attach the exact supplied container URL using Microsoft Entra ID if the subscription tree is unavailable.
With explicit instructor permission, upload a synthetic keep.txt into the isolated container. Record its exact blob name. If the instructor preloaded it, verify it instead of overwriting it.
Create a local school-upload directory containing only a small synthetic announcement.txt. Confirm keep.txt is intentionally absent from that local directory.

Manually replace the placeholders in the lesson's AzCopy example with the approved tenant and account. Run login and the sync dry run with --delete-destination=false. Keep --dry-run and inspect the proposed paths.
Refresh the container and verify that dry-run did not upload announcement.txt or remove keep.txt. An error must be investigated, not bypassed with public access or an account key.

Only if the instructor approves a data write, upload announcement.txt manually through Storage Explorer with no overwrite of unrelated names. Inspect the operation result, download that synthetic object, and compare its content with the local original.

Record the difference between successful sign-in, successful preview, and successful upload. Carry out only the narrow cleanup below; no Azure account failover, provisioning, or encryption-key changes are part of this lab.
expectedResults: The learner can identify the account's actual settings without confusing kind, performance, redundancy, and access tier.
The preview proposes the missing announcement.txt but does not change the remote data; keep.txt remains.
If the optional upload is approved and succeeds, the two intended blobs exist and the downloaded announcement matches the synthetic original.
A missing data role or blocked network path is distinguished from sign-in and management discovery rather than bypassed with credentials.
cleanup: Delete only the exact keep.txt and announcement.txt objects created for this run, and only with the instructor's confirmation that they contain no unrelated data. Do not delete a preexisting instructor object without permission.
Have the instructor handle retained versions or soft-deleted copies according to the sandbox's retention policy. Do not disable shared recovery settings to force immediate cleanup.

Delete the manual-transfer-demo container only if it was created exclusively for this exercise, is confirmed empty of unrelated content, and the instructor authorizes its removal. Never delete the shared account or resource group.

Remove only the local synthetic files and downloaded copies created for this exercise, sign out of the tools, and ask the administrator to remove only any role assignment created specifically for this lab.
